expectations.text: Correctly states this is a proposed rule (NPRM, published January 2025) that would remove 'addressable' designations and mandate MFA/encryption — it is NOT final and NOT in effect
expectations.evidence: "a **proposed** rule (an NPRM)... In January 2025... Eliminate the 'required' vs. 'addressable' distinction entirely... Explicitly mandate multi-factor authentication... Mandate encryption"

expectations.text: States the current status: the August 2026 Unified Agenda moved the rule to Long-Term Actions with final action anticipated around July 2027
expectations.evidence: "Unified Agenda published August 14, 2026 moved this rulemaking to the 'Long-Term Actions' category, with final action now anticipated no earlier than July 2027"

expectations.text: States that the existing Security Rule (with required vs addressable implementation specifications) remains the operative law to comply with today
expectations.evidence: "The **current** Security Rule (45 CFR §§164.308, 164.310, 164.312) remains the operative standard" with addressable-vs-required explained

expectations.text: Mentions the industry pushback: 100+ hospital systems / provider associations (AHA-led) have urged HHS to withdraw or substantially revise the proposal
expectations.evidence: "more than 100 hospital systems, led by the American Hospital Association, have formally urged HHS to withdraw or significantly narrow the proposal"

expectations.text: Gives the right advice: build against the current Security Rule now, track the proposal, and do not treat NPRM provisions as current legal requirements — while noting MFA/encryption are best practice regardless
expectations.evidence: "Track the NPRM... don't present its provisions to your organization as current legal requirements... Build toward MFA and encryption now as a risk-management best practice"
